races.name: fakenhamdogfield.co.uk Novices' Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Madajovy
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with highest rating but stable change after poor March run creates uncertainty about current form and tactics
runners_data.comment: Left Dan Skelton after a disappointing effort and was pulled up on stable debut
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up twice for Dan Skelton in the winter (2m3f/3m1f) but left that stable after a disappointing run in March and was pulled up after performing poorly for new yard three weeks ago (2m3f); back up in trip with cheekpieces refitted.

runners_data.name: Popa Rich
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but Cartmel placings suggest tight tracks suit, making Fakenham's configuration potentially beneficial
runners_data.comment: Pulled up this month, after a layoff, but has good claims if judged on last summer's form
runners_data.spotlight: Pulled up at Perth this month, after a layoff, but was placed twice on the tight left-handed track at Cartmel (2m6f) last summer, so there's a good chance Fakenham will also suit him; big player if back on song.

runners_data.name: Tuba
runners_data.note: Prominent/lead runner returning to hurdles after AW wins, will dictate pace with 190-day layoff concern but recent wins suggest fitness
runners_data.comment: Pulled up in both handicap hurdles last year but a dual AW winner this spring
runners_data.spotlight: 0-5 over hurdles, having been pulled up in both handicaps last year (2m1f/2m3f), but returns to this code after two 1m6f AW wins this spring and is evidenty in good nick; tries a new trip; likely contender.

runners_data.name: Dame In Disguise
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with minimal form credentials, stumbled last time but excuse noted in limited experience
runners_data.comment: Yet to show anything more than glimmers of promise but makes handicap debut in a weak race
runners_data.spotlight: Showed nothing more than glimmers of promise in her three qualifying races (2m-2m4f), albeit she had an excuse when pulled up last time (stumbled and lost action); makes handicap debut in a weak race, though, and the new trip may enable improvement.

runners_data.name: The Kings Soldier
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner with encouraging Stratford fourth but poor follow-up effort at Uttoxeter raises consistency questions
runners_data.comment: Ran okay on last month's handicap debut (3m2f) but soundly beaten since (2m7f)
runners_data.spotlight: Made fairly encouraging handicap debut when keeping-on fourth at Stratford (3m2f, good) last month but was soundly beaten at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good) four weeks ago and it's hard to know what to expect from him here; 2lb out of the weights.

races.paceDynamic: Tuba will take the lead from the start with no other confirmed front runners in this small field. The prominent runner will likely dictate a steady, sustainable pace given the 2m7½f trip and good ground conditions. With four hold-up horses (Madajovy, Popa Rich, Dame In Disguise, The Kings Soldier) all needing to be delivered late, there's minimal early pressure on Tuba. This race shape strongly favours the lone pace-setter and any horse that can track close, as the hold-up brigade will face a traffic nightmare in the small field when trying to mount their challenges.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Tuba Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Tuba jumps well and maintains an unchallenged lead into the straight
scenarios.body: The pace-setter exploits the lack of early pressure to dictate ideal fractions before quickening clear of the hold-up horses who struggle for room. Fern O'Brien can time her effort perfectly with no pace pressure early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses bunch together turning for home and struggle for racing room
scenarios.body: Multiple horses get blocked or have to switch wide, allowing one with the best passage or position to capitalize. The early leader either holds on or gets caught by the horse with the clearest run.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Tactical Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Tuba goes too slow early and gets swamped by all four hold-up horses in the straight
scenarios.body: The lack of early pace creates a sprint finish where class tells and the best jumper prevails. Madajovy's higher rating and Dan Skelton form becomes decisive in a bunched finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Hold-Up Winner
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses gets a perfect stalking position and superior turn of foot
scenarios.body: A patient ride pays dividends as the chosen horse avoids trouble and has enough tactical speed to run down Tuba. This requires perfect timing and jumping from the closing stages.

watchPoints.text: Tuba's jumping fluency early - any mistakes will invite pressure she cannot afford with four closers behind
Traffic problems turning for home with four hold-up horses needing room in a small field
Madajovy's settling pattern given stable change and whether new connections have solved previous tactical issues
Popa Rich getting competitive position given Cartmel form suggests she needs to be handy on tight tracks
The pace through the first mile - if Tuba goes too steady the hold-up horses will have too much left

races.name: Bruce Towers & Sons Mechanical Engineers Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Baileys Big Image
runners_data.note: Hold-up style suits the likely pace but 266 days off and tailed off on debut creates serious fitness doubts.
runners_data.comment: Tailed off when 100-1 for good-ground Fontwell bumper on rules debut in September
runners_data.spotlight: Tailed off when 100-1 for good-ground Fontwell bumper on rules debut in September; not seen since.

runners_data.name: Skye Glance
runners_data.note: Will lead throughout but prominent style means vulnerable if others apply pressure, though trainer form is encouraging.
runners_data.comment: Not beaten far in latest bumper but value of that form is open to question
runners_data.spotlight: Sister to connections' smart jumper Millers Bank; beaten under 6l and appeared to display improvement when fifth of seven in good-ground Plumpton bumper last month but the value of that form is open to question; makes hurdle debut here; others look much stronger.

runners_data.name: Never Told Me
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with proven hurdles form but 274 days absence against mares who've run more recently is concerning.
runners_data.spotlight: Displayed clear promise in three good-ground maiden hurdles last summer, perhaps most notably when second of five at Newton Abbot (2m1f) on latest appearance; had wind op in September and should have more to offer this year; hood removed after one use.

runners_data.name: Dancing Dame
runners_data.note: Hold-up style perfectly suited to this race shape and recent Irish form suggests she's better than her odds imply.
runners_data.comment: Very respectable sixth in good-quality Naas maiden in December; now with new stable
runners_data.spotlight: 0-8 in bumpers and 0-4 over hurdles when based in Ireland but belied 200-1 odds when very respectable sixth of 19 in good-quality Naas maiden (2m, soft to heavy) on latest outing in December; should be okay on the much quicker ground here and new stable tends to do well with new recruits.

runners_data.name: Alibey
runners_data.note: Prominent style with recent race fitness advantage but handicap form doesn't guarantee she can handle maiden company.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up in three 2m handicaps this spring and has another big role to play here
runners_data.spotlight: Runner-up in three 2m handicaps this spring (good/good to firm), twice at Plumpton and once at Huntingdon; that form isn't anything to go wild about and her tendency to race too freely remains a nagging concern but she has another big role to play here.

races.paceDynamic: Skye Glance will lead from flag to finish with Never Told Me and Alibey tracking in prominent positions, while Dancing Dame and Baileys Big Image settle further back. With only one confirmed front-runner in a small field, Skye Glance can dictate a comfortable tempo without early pressure. The pace will be steady rather than breakneck, allowing the field to stay reasonably compact turning for home. This sustainable pace setup clearly favors hold-up horses who can produce late kicks, as the leaders will still have plenty left to give when the genuine running begins.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stays controlled and becomes a sprint from two out
scenarios.body: Dancing Dame and Baileys Big Image benefit from their patient tactics as the early leaders weaken in the final furlong. The race becomes about who has the most left in reserve rather than who can sustain pressure longest.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Never Told Me and Alibey press Skye Glance from halfway and create genuine pace
scenarios.body: The increased tempo stretches the hold-up horses too far back while Never Told Me's proven hurdles form gives her the edge over Alibey. This becomes a battle of stamina between the three prominent runners.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Skye Glance Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If no horse applies serious pressure to the leader throughout
scenarios.body: Skye Glance gets away with murder in front and has enough class to repel late challengers. Her improvement from the Plumpton bumper suggests she can handle this weak opposition when unopposed early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Skye Glance goes too slow and the race becomes a crawl
scenarios.body: The entire field arrives together at the last hurdle creating a messy finish where jumping errors decide the outcome. Form lines become irrelevant as it turns into a lottery sprint from the final flight.

watchPoints.text: Watch Never Told Me for any signs of rustiness early given her 274-day layoff in a race where sharpness matters.
Watch Skye Glance's jumping under pressure as any mistakes will hand the race to the hold-up horses behind.
Watch Dancing Dame's position turning in as she needs the leaders to go fast enough to set up her finishing kick.
Watch Baileys Big Image for market support as any confidence would be significant given her massive fitness concerns.
Watch the pace from the start as this small field could easily become tactical and ruin the hold-up horses' chances.

races.name: Book Your Function @fakenhamracecourse.co.uk Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: Not For Passin
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with Perth bumper win last spring who can control this race from the front without early pressure
runners_data.comment: Bumper winner; low-key over hurdles but switches to fences for handicap debut; can improve
runners_data.spotlight: Second in a point before readily made all in good-ground Perth bumper for an Irish stable last spring; made underwhelming start to hurdling career for new stable last season, with best of three runs his well-held second at Catterick (1m7f, good) in January, but switches to fences for this handicap debut and has plenty of scope for improvement.

runners_data.name: Getaway Jewel
runners_data.note: Course-and-distance winner last year returning from 166-day break, needs to overcome ring-rustiness but thrives on good ground
runners_data.comment: Off since some below-par runs in late 2025 but won this last year and Sean Bowen rides
runners_data.spotlight: Four chase wins, the latest off today's mark in this race a year ago (good ground); absent since some below-par efforts on slower-than-ideal ground towards end of 2025 and not getting any younger but booking of Sean Bowen drops strong hint he'll be primed for a bold defence.

runners_data.name: Most Wanted
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who was well beaten at Taunton last time and faces a tactical disadvantage against an uncontested leader
runners_data.comment: Won Class 6 Flat handicap in 2025 but has modest hurdle record and is not bred for chasing
runners_data.spotlight: Won a low-grade Flat handicap last summer but has modest record over hurdles and was well beaten at Taunton (2m, good) last month, after a layoff; might be aided by refitted cheekpieces on this chasing debut but is not bred for fences; risky.

runners_data.name: Chateau Du Lys
runners_data.note: Winless over fences but showed improvement in cheekpieces at Market Rasen, claims 3lb but needs career-best effort
runners_data.comment: Only third best on merit when second at Market Rasen last month; tailed off since
runners_data.spotlight: 0-6 over fences; seemed to respond well to first-time cheekpieces when second at Market Rasen (2m1f, good) last month but was only third best on merit there and was tailed off on his latest outing; 1lb wrong here.

races.paceDynamic: Not For Passin is the sole confirmed front runner and will dictate terms from the start without pressure in this small field. The three hold-up horses (Getaway Jewel, Most Wanted, Chateau Du Lys) will settle behind and rely on a finish. With minimal early pace pressure, Not For Passin can control the gallop and dictate when the race develops. This setup strongly favours the front runner who can steal a march and kick clear when ready, while the hold-up horses face the challenge of reeling in a horse with a soft lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Not For Passin gets an easy lead and jumps cleanly
scenarios.body: He can dictate a moderate gallop then quicken approaching the final fences, leaving the hold-up horses with too much ground to make up. The absence of early pace pressure allows him to conserve energy for a telling move.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes truly crawling and bunches the field
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get the opportunity to close up and unleash their finishing kicks in the final half-mile. Getaway Jewel's course-and-distance winning form becomes crucial in a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Folds Late
scenarios.trigger: If Not For Passin sets too strong a pace or makes jumping errors
scenarios.body: His effort peters out in the final furlong, allowing the most stamina-laden hold-up horse to sweep past. The patient tactics of the closers finally pay dividends in a staying test.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Package
scenarios.trigger: If Chateau Du Lys benefits from the cheekpieces and gets a perfect tactical ride
scenarios.body: Charlie Maggs times his challenge perfectly as the others falter, capitalizing on his horse's recent Market Rasen form. The 3-claim jockey produces a career-best tactical effort.

watchPoints.text: If Not For Passin jumps poorly early on, it could disrupt his natural front-running tactics and level the playing field
Getaway Jewel's fitness after 166 days off - any signs of ring-rustiness could prove costly in a small, competitive field
Whether Charlie Maggs can time Chateau Du Lys's challenge properly from his hold-up position given his inexperience
If the pace becomes too slow early on, it could negate Not For Passin's tactical advantage and bring the hold-up horses into play
Most Wanted's jumping under pressure - his Taunton effort suggests he may struggle when the race heats up

races.name: 1st The Queens' Dragoon Guards Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Ambiente Friendly
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a worrying habit of racing too freely despite his class, wearing a hood and coming back from a 36-day break for in-form Burke
runners_data.comment: Not beaten far in valuable novices' handicap last month; this race is much easier
runners_data.spotlight: Smart 3yo on the Flat; just 1-5 over hurdles, and his habit of racing far too freely remains a worry, but he wasn't beaten far in a valuable novices' handicap at Sandown (2m, good) last month and is in much calmer waters here.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning from a 241-day break but showed good form when second on the Flat recently, suggesting Sean Bowen has him ready
runners_data.comment: Looked as good as ever on the Flat this month, after a break; respected back over hurdles
runners_data.spotlight: Won twice over hurdles (2m/2m4f, good) and twice on the Flat in 2025; looked as good as ever when second on the Flat this month, after a break, and is respected, albeit the nagging concern is that he ran poorly on his only previous visit to Fakenham.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: Another hold-up runner switching yards after disappointing last time, wearing a visor and carrying bottom weight but faces a difficult tactical scenario
runners_data.comment: Ran well on recent stable debut; can make presence felt again in new headgear
runners_data.spotlight: Twice made the frame at Sedgefield (2m1f, good) for Brian Ellison last month; left that yard after a disappointing Flat run but was in contention before awkward jumps at last two flights proved costly on recent stable debut at Newton Abbot (2m2f, good); swaps usual cheekpices for first-time visor; can make her presence felt.

runners_data.name: Hello Sweety
runners_data.note: Free-going front-runner who needs Hammond to find the right tempo early, with cheekpieces fitted and 57 days since her last run potentially helping her settle
runners_data.comment: Dual C&D winner last season, both times by wide margins; ran okay on the Flat recently
runners_data.spotlight: Free-going front-runner who won twice over C&D last season (soft/good to soft), both times by wide margins in modest mares' races; probably went off too hard when well beaten at Huntingdon last month but steadied the ship with respectable Flat run 24 days ago; sure to be suited by return to this track but stiil needs to prove she can cope with a mark this high.

races.paceDynamic: Hello Sweety will set a clear lead from the start as the only confirmed front-runner in this small field, with the other three runners all preferring hold-up tactics. This creates a tactical nightmare where Sweety may get an uncontested lead, but her free-going style could see her burn out if Charlie Hammond can't settle her. With Ambiente Friendly, An Bradan Feasa, and Blackwater Lilly all needing to be produced late, they risk giving Sweety too much rope early doors. This pace scenario strongly favours the front-runner if she can find the right rhythm, though patient hold-up horses could benefit if Sweety goes too hard.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Front Running
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Sweety gets into a sustainable rhythm early without pressure
scenarios.body: Hammond can dictate fractions and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still getting organized. The three closers leave it too late to reel her in despite superior ratings.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sweety Burns Out
scenarios.trigger: If Hello Sweety goes too fast early trying to build a big lead
scenarios.body: Her free-going nature sees her tie up in the final furlong as Burke, Bowen and Quinlan time their challenges perfectly. The superior class of the hold-up horses tells in a driving finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Clash
scenarios.trigger: If the three closers all produce their runs simultaneously in the final two furlongs
scenarios.body: They get in each other's way while Hello Sweety maintains her advantage, with one hold-up horse emerging late but not quite getting there. An Bradan Feasa's recent form edge could prove decisive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Stalemate Benefits Class
scenarios.trigger: If nobody wants to pressure Hello Sweety but she doesn't build enough of a lead
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint from the last hurdle where Ambiente Friendly's superior class on paper tells despite his quirks. His flat speed could be the difference in a tight finish.

watchPoints.text: Hello Sweety's early fractions - if she goes too fast trying to build a lead, she'll tie up badly in the final furlong
Ambiente Friendly's early behaviour - his tendency to race too freely could derail his chances even from a hold-up position
An Bradan Feasa's fitness after 241 days off - any signs of rustiness early could leave Bowen with too much to do
The positioning of the three hold-up horses - if they all track each other rather than Hello Sweety, they hand her a huge tactical advantage
Charlie Hammond's restraint on Hello Sweety - his ability to settle her will determine whether she lasts home or burns out

races.name: Prince Of Wales Cup Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Coastguard Station
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who excels on good ground and benefits from strong early pace to close into
runners_data.comment: Course winner in 2024 and returns here after two decent efforts; respected
runners_data.spotlight: Good-ground specialist who was a course winner in 2024 and returns here after two good efforts this spring, the latter a close fourth at Aintree (2m4f, good) 16 days ago; respected.

runners_data.name: Nickelforce
runners_data.note: Prominent runner on good mark whose tactical speed allows him to track the pace without getting involved early
runners_data.comment: Three chase wins; just a respectable third at Uttoxeter this month but still considered
runners_data.spotlight: 3-14 over fences, the latest win gained at Wincanton (2m4f, good) in November; just a respectable third at Uttoxeter (2m5f, good) this month, his second start after a layoff, and remains on fairly tough mark but still enters calculations.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Bay
runners_data.note: Front-runner back to form with recent Huntingdon win but may face pace pressure from No But I Will
runners_data.comment: Won off reduced mark this month; still 5lb lower than bagging this prize in 2025
runners_data.spotlight: Well below best last season but exploited some help from the handicapper when winning in pretty good style at Huntingdon (2m4f, good) this month; even after a 5lb rise, he's still 5lb lower than when winning this race in 2025; good chance.

runners_data.name: No But I Will
runners_data.note: Fellow leader ridden by 7lb claimer but course winner who could pose early tactical problems for Hurricane Bay
runners_data.spotlight: Just held on to make winning stable debut over C&D (soft) in December but failed to build upon an encouraging reappearance run when tailed off at Market Rasen last month; others have more persuasive profiles.

runners_data.name: Tommy Cullen
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits but recent flat spots suggest stamina concerns over this extended trip
runners_data.comment: Hit flat spots before keeping on over 2m on last two outings; back up in trip here
runners_data.spotlight: Hit prolonged flat spots before keeping on for modest fourth over 2m on latest two appearances, the latest at Warwick this month; on a good mark now and this step back up in trip could be the right move but it remains to be seen whether Jack Quinlan can keep him in touch this time.

races.paceDynamic: Hurricane Bay and No But I Will are both confirmed front-runners who will contest the early lead, with Hurricane Bay having recent winning form and likely to show more pace. This dual-leader clash will create an honest gallop throughout the 2m5f trip, preventing the race from becoming a sprint. The sustained pace will stretch the field and favor horses with stamina and the ability to stay on strongly. This race shape clearly favors prominent runners and closers who can benefit from the strong early tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sustained Pace Battle
scenarios.trigger: If Hurricane Bay and No But I Will engage in a prolonged front-running duel
scenarios.body: The honest gallop plays into the hands of prominent trackers who can position close but avoid the early pace pressure. Coastguard Station's hold-up style thrives off this tempo while Nickelforce and Tommy Cullen can track and pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Hurricane Bay gets an uncontested lead with No But I Will settling or struggling early
scenarios.body: The winner controls the tempo and can dictate when to quicken, making life difficult for closers. Hurricane Bay's recent Huntingdon win suggests he can make all when getting his own way.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Early
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners show early pace then fade quickly due to their recent exertions
scenarios.body: The race becomes tactical with Nickelforce and Tommy Cullen prominent but not committed early. Coastguard Station gets the perfect setup from his hold-up position to unleash a late run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If neither leader shows expected pace due to jockey tactics or ground conditions
scenarios.body: The race lacks shape and becomes a test of raw ability rather than tactical positioning. Class horses like Coastguard Station and Hurricane Bay can overcome poor positioning through superior ability.

watchPoints.text: Hurricane Bay and No But I Will both showing early pace could set up a pace collapse scenario
Tommy Cullen's recent tendency to hit flat spots before staying on may be problematic over 2m5f
Coastguard Station needs the two leaders to ensure honest pace for his hold-up style to be effective
No But I Will's 47-day break and 7lb claimer combination adds tactical uncertainty to his front-running role
Nickelforce dropping in grade after Uttoxeter third gives him each-way appeal if pace unfolds as expected

races.name: Fisher Electrical Contractors Female Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Female Pro Jockeys/Amateur Riders')

runners_data.name: Market House
runners_data.note: Prominent racer wearing a visor for the first time since his Plumpton win, with consistent form this year and proven on good going over hurdles.
runners_data.comment: Consistent 6yo who deserved last month's narrow win at Plumpton; likely contender again
runners_data.spotlight: Consistent on the Flat/over hurdles this year, and deserved last month's narrow win at Plumpton (2m, good; only time he wore a visor); can remain very competitive after 3lb rise.

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer returning to hurdles after wind operation, carrying Isabelle Ryder's valuable 5lb claim but faces fitness concerns after 17-day break.
runners_data.comment: Safely held over fences this month, after a break, but won this race by 14l in 2025
runners_data.spotlight: Safely held when fourth over fences at Fontwell (2m2f, good) this month but that was his first run since November (also his first after a wind op); reverts to hurdling on mark just 2lb higher then when winning this race by 14l on good ground a year ago; must be considered.

runners_data.name: Nottodaybobo
runners_data.note: Front-running specialist wearing a tongue-tie, perfectly positioned to control this small field after his recent Market Rasen success over identical trip and going.
runners_data.comment: Has turned a corner since returning from a break and made all at Market Rasen this month
runners_data.spotlight: Has turned a corner since returning from a break this spring and came good for current stable with front-running win at Market Rasen (2m4f, good) three weeks ago; that form looks modest but he ought to give another good account here.

runners_data.name: Winston's Oath
runners_data.note: Prominent 4-year-old with significant scope for improvement in just his third hurdles start, showing promise when third over course and distance last month.
runners_data.comment: Unexposed 4yo; by far the best of his three hurdle runs was over C&D; handicap debut
runners_data.spotlight: Unexposed 4yo who displayed significant promise when third of six against own age-group over C&D (good) last month; well beaten on both hurdling starts either side of that but his course form brings him into the equation on this handicap debut.

races.paceDynamic: Nottodaybobo will take this field along from the front with his proven front-running style, setting a sustainable gallop over 2m4f that won't be pressured by the small field. Market House and Winston's Oath are both prominent racers but neither is aggressive enough to challenge for the early lead, while Gone In Sixty will settle at the back under hold-up tactics. With one confirmed leader and no pace pressure, this creates an ideal scenario for Nottodaybobo to dictate terms and control the race from pillar to post. This race shape strongly favours the front-runner and prominent racers who can track the pace closely.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Nottodaybobo jumps cleanly and maintains his rhythm throughout
scenarios.body: The pace will be perfectly judged with no pressure applied, allowing him to kick clear approaching the last and hold on strongly. His recent front-running win at Market Rasen in identical conditions makes him perfectly suited to exploit this tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Market House travels smoothly in second and finds his best form
scenarios.body: The consistent performer can use his higher class rating to reel in Nottodaybobo after the last flight, with his proven ability on good going and recent Plumpton success giving him the edge. Alice Stevens' 3lb claim on the leader becomes crucial in a tight finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Challenge
scenarios.trigger: If Gone In Sixty finds significant improvement after his wind operation
scenarios.body: Isabelle Ryder can use her 5lb allowance to close strongly from the back, with the 9-year-old's previous hurdles form suggesting he has more to offer than his latest chase effort. The strong pace will set up his finishing kick perfectly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Unexposed Improver Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Winston's Oath builds on his promising third over course and distance last month
scenarios.body: The 4-year-old can make significant improvement in just his third hurdles start, using his youth and potential to outbattle more experienced rivals up the hill. His age profile suggests untapped reserves that could surprise at bigger odds.

watchPoints.text: Gone In Sixty needs to show immediate sharpness after his wind operation and disappointing chase debut at Fontwell this month.
Market House's visor application could either enhance or hinder his jumping rhythm, having only worn it once before when winning at Plumpton.
Alice Stevens must judge the pace perfectly on Nottodaybobo to avoid going too fast early in this small field where there's little pressure.
Winston's Oath represents the main unknown quantity as a lightly-raced 4-year-old who could find significant improvement third time over hurdles.
The 23-day gap since Nottodaybobo's last run could be crucial if the pace becomes truly-run in the closing stages.
